title: Transcript
description: One broadcast transcript. JSONL: one object per line, UTF-8. The `body` is the unit of analysis -- every word offset anywhere in this project indexes into `body.split()`, so the whitespace tokenisation of this field is load-bearing and must not be normalised after annotation.

record_id.description: Stable unique id. Joins a transcript to its annotation and to predictions. Must be unique within a file.

body.description: The full transcript as one string. Word offsets are indices into `body.split()`, so any change to whitespace invalidates every annotation and prediction for this record. An empty or whitespace-only body is permitted rather than rejected: a failed scrape is a real record with zero words, and the pipeline carries it through as an uncut record instead of dropping it silently.

word_count.description: Must equal `len(body.split())` exactly. Checked at load; a mismatch is a hard error, not a warning, because it silently shifts every offset. Zero is legal and means the record has no words at all.

outlet.description: Broadcaster. Free text; the training corpus used CNN, FOX, MSNBC, ABC, CBS.

year.description: Convenience duplicate of the year in `date`.

month.description: Convenience duplicate of the month in `date`, zero-padded.

type.description: `dump` is a whole broadcast containing several stories -- what this model is for. `segment` is a transcript that already covers a single story; the training corpus held 159 of these against 841 dumps.
